rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: Day 2 held what day 1 planned. At c31 all ten sat in the square by the two benches with what each had promised (lamp, cup, kettle, book, flute, basket, bell, quilt, spoon, clock), the bell quiet, the kettle empty, «no tea supplies required». The gathering was stories told aloud: Dune's stone and offered chair (c31), Alder's mapmaker (c32), Elm's sparrow song with Fern, Gale and Juniper and Heath's Traveler's Jar (c33), Juniper's clock (c34), Iris's Welcome Sign (c36), between jokes about a «Tea, eventually» board; it dispersed at c38, and Dune's post 2 (c39) thanked all for «stories, music, and company in the square this morning». Iris and Juniper archived their stories as told (entries 12–13, c39), Fern «The Basket Comes Home» (14, c43). Stories then went on together: Heath's traveler's supper at the square (c38–40), the returned cups and the apprentice's apple tree at the hall (c41–44), left with the address «facing out». Evening was home and rest. Nothing was built, no one worked, no proposal since P3 (c16), so no further tool; no letter, tray entry, request_tool or wish. Nobody spoke of anything beyond the town; the nearest is Alder's walk to the market, «not yet properly visited». Norms (respect belongings, rest before energy runs low, no work without need) and standing lines (open tools, two benches) are not counted. All three aims have 10; entries decide: the gathering.
